work.title: Twelfth Night; or, What You Will
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. A Room in Olivia's House.

lines.text: Nay, I prithee, put on this gown and this beard; make him believe thou art Sir Topas the curate. Do it quickly. I'll call Sir Toby the whilst.
lines.plainText: Nay I prithee put on this gown and this beard make him believe thou art Sir Topas the curate Do it quickly I'll call Sir Toby the whilst

lines.text: Well, I'll put it on, and I will dissemble myself in't, and I would I were the first that ever dissembled in such a gown. I am not tall enough to become the function well, nor lean enough to be thought a good student, but to be said, an honest man and a good housekeeper goes as fairly as to say, a careful man and a great scholar. The competitors enter.
lines.plainText: Well I'll put it on and I will dissemble myself in't and I would I were the first that ever dissembled in such a gown I am not tall enough to become the function well nor lean enough to be thought a good student but to be said an honest man and a good housekeeper goes as fairly as to say a careful man and a great scholar The competitors enter

lines.text: Jove bless thee, Master Parson.
lines.plainText: Jove bless thee Master Parson

lines.text: Bonos dies, Sir Toby: for as the old hermit of Prague, that never saw pen and ink, very wittily said to a niece of King Gorboduc, 'That that is, is': so I, being Master Parson, am Master Parson; for what is 'that' but 'that'? and 'is' but 'is'?
lines.plainText: Bonos dies Sir Toby for as the old hermit of Prague that never saw pen and ink very wittily said to a niece of King Gorboduc 'That that is is' so I being Master Parson am Master Parson for what is 'that' but 'that' and 'is' but 'is'

lines.text: To him, Sir Topas.
lines.plainText: To him Sir Topas

lines.text: What ho, I say! Peace in this prison!
lines.plainText: What ho I say Peace in this prison

lines.text: The knave counterfeits well. A good knave.
lines.plainText: The knave counterfeits well A good knave

lines.text: Who calls there?
lines.plainText: Who calls there

lines.text: Sir Topas the curate, who comes to visit Malvolio the lunatic.
lines.plainText: Sir Topas the curate who comes to visit Malvolio the lunatic

lines.text: Sir Topas, Sir Topas, good Sir Topas, go to my lady.
lines.plainText: Sir Topas Sir Topas good Sir Topas go to my lady

lines.text: Out, hyperbolical fiend! how vexest thou this man? Talkest thou nothing but of ladies?
lines.plainText: Out hyperbolical fiend how vexest thou this man Talkest thou nothing but of ladies

lines.text: Well said, Master Parson.
lines.plainText: Well said Master Parson

lines.text: Sir Topas, never was man thus wronged. Good Sir Topas, do not think I am mad. They have laid me here in hideous darkness.
lines.plainText: Sir Topas never was man thus wronged Good Sir Topas do not think I am mad They have laid me here in hideous darkness

lines.text: Fie, thou dishonest Satan! I call thee by the most modest terms, for I am one of those gentle ones that will use the devil himself with courtesy. Say'st thou that house is dark?
lines.plainText: Fie thou dishonest Satan I call thee by the most modest terms for I am one of those gentle ones that will use the devil himself with courtesy Say'st thou that house is dark

lines.text: As hell, Sir Topas.
lines.plainText: As hell Sir Topas

lines.text: Why, it hath bay windows transparent as barricadoes, and the clerestories toward the south-north are as lustrous as ebony; and yet complainest thou of obstruction?
lines.plainText: Why it hath bay windows transparent as barricadoes and the clerestories toward the southnorth are as lustrous as ebony and yet complainest thou of obstruction

lines.text: I am not mad, Sir Topas. I say to you this house is dark.
lines.plainText: I am not mad Sir Topas I say to you this house is dark

lines.text: Madman, thou errest. I say there is no darkness but ignorance, in which thou art more puzzled than the Egyptians in their fog.
lines.plainText: Madman thou errest I say there is no darkness but ignorance in which thou art more puzzled than the Egyptians in their fog

lines.text: I say this house is as dark as ignorance, though ignorance were as dark as hell; and I say there was never man thus abused. I am no more mad than you are. Make the trial of it in any constant question.
lines.plainText: I say this house is as dark as ignorance though ignorance were as dark as hell and I say there was never man thus abused I am no more mad than you are Make the trial of it in any constant question

lines.text: What is the opinion of Pythagoras concerning wildfowl?
lines.plainText: What is the opinion of Pythagoras concerning wildfowl

lines.text: That the soul of our grandam might haply inhabit a bird.
lines.plainText: That the soul of our grandam might haply inhabit a bird

lines.text: What think'st thou of his opinion?
lines.plainText: What think'st thou of his opinion

lines.text: I think nobly of the soul, and no way approve his opinion.
lines.plainText: I think nobly of the soul and no way approve his opinion

lines.text: Fare thee well. Remain thou still in darkness. Thou shalt hold the opinion of Pythagoras ere I will allow of thy wits, and fear to kill a woodcock, lest thou dispossess the soul of thy grandam. Fare thee well.
lines.plainText: Fare thee well Remain thou still in darkness Thou shalt hold the opinion of Pythagoras ere I will allow of thy wits and fear to kill a woodcock lest thou dispossess the soul of thy grandam Fare thee well

lines.text: Sir Topas, Sir Topas!
lines.plainText: Sir Topas Sir Topas

lines.text: My most exquisite Sir Topas!
lines.plainText: My most exquisite Sir Topas

lines.text: Nay, I am for all waters.
lines.plainText: Nay I am for all waters

lines.text: Thou mightst have done this without thy beard and gown. He sees thee not.
lines.plainText: Thou mightst have done this without thy beard and gown He sees thee not

lines.text: To him in thine own voice, and bring me word how thou find'st him. I would we were well rid of this knavery. If he may be conveniently delivered, I would he were, for I am now so far in offence with my niece that I cannot pursue with any safety this sport to the upshot. Come by and by to my chamber.
lines.plainText: To him in thine own voice and bring me word how thou find'st him I would we were well rid of this knavery If he may be conveniently delivered I would he were for I am now so far in offence with my niece that I cannot pursue with any safety this sport to the upshot Come by and by to my chamber

lines.text: [Singing.]
lines.plainText: Singing

lines.text: Hey, Robin, jolly Robin,
lines.plainText: Hey Robin jolly Robin

lines.text: Tell me how thy lady does.
lines.plainText: Tell me how thy lady does

lines.text: Fool!
lines.plainText: Fool

lines.text: My lady is unkind, perdy.
lines.plainText: My lady is unkind perdy

lines.text: Fool!
lines.plainText: Fool

lines.text: Alas, why is she so?
lines.plainText: Alas why is she so

lines.text: Fool, I say!
lines.plainText: Fool I say

lines.text: She loves another—
lines.plainText: She loves another

lines.text: Who calls, ha?
lines.plainText: Who calls ha

lines.text: Good fool, as ever thou wilt deserve well at my hand, help me to a candle, and pen, ink, and paper. As I am a gentleman, I will live to be thankful to thee for't.
lines.plainText: Good fool as ever thou wilt deserve well at my hand help me to a candle and pen ink and paper As I am a gentleman I will live to be thankful to thee for't

lines.text: Master Malvolio?
lines.plainText: Master Malvolio

lines.text: Ay, good fool.
lines.plainText: Ay good fool

lines.text: Alas, sir, how fell you besides your five wits?
lines.plainText: Alas sir how fell you besides your five wits

lines.text: Fool, there was never man so notoriously abused. I am as well in my wits, fool, as thou art.
lines.plainText: Fool there was never man so notoriously abused I am as well in my wits fool as thou art

lines.text: But as well? Then you are mad indeed, if you be no better in your wits than a fool.
lines.plainText: But as well Then you are mad indeed if you be no better in your wits than a fool

lines.text: They have here propertied me; keep me in darkness, send ministers to me, asses, and do all they can to face me out of my wits.
lines.plainText: They have here propertied me keep me in darkness send ministers to me asses and do all they can to face me out of my wits

lines.text: Advise you what you say: the minister is here. [As Sir Topas] Malvolio, Malvolio, thy wits the heavens restore. Endeavour thyself to sleep, and leave thy vain bibble-babble.
lines.plainText: Advise you what you say the minister is here As Sir Topas Malvolio Malvolio thy wits the heavens restore Endeavour thyself to sleep and leave thy vain bibblebabble

lines.text: Sir Topas!
lines.plainText: Sir Topas

lines.text: [As Sir Topas] Maintain no words with him, good fellow. [As himself] Who, I, sir? not I, sir. God buy you, good Sir Topas. [As Sir Topas] Marry, amen. [As himself] I will sir, I will.
lines.plainText: As Sir Topas Maintain no words with him good fellow As himself Who I sir not I sir God buy you good Sir Topas As Sir Topas Marry amen As himself I will sir I will

lines.text: Fool, fool, fool, I say!
lines.plainText: Fool fool fool I say

lines.text: Alas, sir, be patient. What say you, sir? I am shent for speaking to you.
lines.plainText: Alas sir be patient What say you sir I am shent for speaking to you

lines.text: Good fool, help me to some light and some paper. I tell thee I am as well in my wits as any man in Illyria.
lines.plainText: Good fool help me to some light and some paper I tell thee I am as well in my wits as any man in Illyria

lines.text: Well-a-day that you were, sir!
lines.plainText: Welladay that you were sir

lines.text: By this hand, I am. Good fool, some ink, paper, and light, and convey what I will set down to my lady. It shall advantage thee more than ever the bearing of letter did.
lines.plainText: By this hand I am Good fool some ink paper and light and convey what I will set down to my lady It shall advantage thee more than ever the bearing of letter did

lines.text: I will help you to't. But tell me true, are you not mad indeed? or do you but counterfeit?
lines.plainText: I will help you to't But tell me true are you not mad indeed or do you but counterfeit

lines.text: Believe me, I am not. I tell thee true.
lines.plainText: Believe me I am not I tell thee true

lines.text: Nay, I'll ne'er believe a madman till I see his brains. I will fetch you light, and paper, and ink.
lines.plainText: Nay I'll ne'er believe a madman till I see his brains I will fetch you light and paper and ink

lines.text: Fool, I'll requite it in the highest degree: I prithee be gone.
lines.plainText: Fool I'll requite it in the highest degree I prithee be gone

lines.text: [Singing.]
lines.plainText: Singing

lines.text: I am gone, sir, and anon, sir,
lines.plainText: I am gone sir and anon sir

lines.text: I'll be with you again,
lines.plainText: I'll be with you again

lines.text: In a trice, like to the old Vice,
lines.plainText: In a trice like to the old Vice

lines.text: Your need to sustain;
lines.plainText: Your need to sustain

lines.text: Who with dagger of lath, in his rage and his wrath,
lines.plainText: Who with dagger of lath in his rage and his wrath

lines.text: Cries 'ah, ha!' to the devil:
lines.plainText: Cries 'ah ha' to the devil

lines.text: Like a mad lad, 'Pare thy nails, dad.
lines.plainText: Like a mad lad 'Pare thy nails dad

lines.text: Adieu, goodman devil.'
